title: An imitation profile damages real friendships
mechanism_summary: Someone creates a fake account in another person's identity and sends hostile messages to their friends. Recipients attribute the messages to the person being impersonated.
suggested_beats: A copied identity appears online.
Friends receive messages the person never sent.
Verify unusual messages and report the fake account.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone whose identity is copied online
why_it_works: Familiar identity cues can make fabricated messages believable.

title: A fake public profile is designed to humiliate
mechanism_summary: An impostor opens a social account in someone's identity to embarrass them. The profile makes abusive material appear associated with the target.
suggested_beats: A duplicate profile appears.
Its content humiliates the identity holder.
Report impersonation and keep evidence.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone with a public online profile
why_it_works: An apparent first-person account can make humiliation seem self-inflicted.

title: A distant romantic partner invents an emergency
mechanism_summary: A scammer builds a romantic connection through an online persona. An invented medical or travel emergency becomes a request for money.
suggested_beats: A new online relationship grows.
An emergency requires a transfer.
Do not send money to an unverified online partner.
why_it_works: Emotional closeness can make financial requests feel like mutual care.

title: An offshore worker persona explains every absence
mechanism_summary: A romance scammer claims to work somewhere that prevents meeting in person. The fabricated occupation sustains the relationship while money requests follow.
suggested_beats: A new contact claims distant work.
The explanation prevents meeting while requests continue.
Independently question identity and financial claims.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone trusting a remote romantic contact
why_it_works: A credible-sounding absence explains away a major opportunity to verify identity.

title: A military profile borrows trust from service
mechanism_summary: A romance scammer poses as a servicemember through an online account. The false identity supports a relationship that is used to solicit money.
suggested_beats: A service-themed profile makes contact.
Romantic attention becomes a financial request.
Verify identity outside the account.
why_it_works: Respect for service can lend an impostor unearned credibility.

title: A celebrity mimic seeks a private relationship
mechanism_summary: Scam accounts impersonate celebrities to approach people through social media. The apparent personal attention is used as part of a romance scam.
suggested_beats: An apparent celebrity makes contact.
The conversation becomes an intimate approach.
Treat unsolicited celebrity relationships as unverified.
why_it_works: A sense of exceptional access can displace ordinary skepticism.

title: A giveaway winner must pay to collect
mechanism_summary: A social media giveaway message says the recipient has won a prize. The supposed organizer demands payment or financial information to release it.
suggested_beats: A giveaway announces a win.
Collecting requires money or private details.
Verify the organizer and reject prize-payment demands.
why_it_works: The excitement of winning can conceal an impersonator's collection demand.

title: A valuable gift from an online partner needs fees
mechanism_summary: A romance scammer claims to have sent a valuable package. The invented delivery then requires customs or other payments before release.
suggested_beats: An online partner promises a valuable gift.
Clearance charges block its arrival.
Verify the shipment independently before paying.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone trusting gifts promised by an online partner
why_it_works: Romantic trust and anticipated value can normalize repeated fees.
